name: Sydney
tagline: A sparkling harbour city of sails and ferries, with the world's most recognisable opera house, a steel arch, surf beaches within a tram ride and coastal walks along the cliffs.
highlight: A ferry across the harbour at sunset, with the Opera House and the Harbour Bridge lit gold behind you.
shortDescription: Australia's largest city: the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, The Rocks, the Botanic Garden, Bondi and Manly beaches, cliff walks, ferries and a lively food and café scene.
metaDescription: A Sydney travel guide: the Opera House, Harbour Bridge and BridgeClimb, The Rocks, Bondi to Coogee coastal walk, Manly ferry, Royal Botanic Garden, food, where to stay and a three-day plan.
knownFor: The Opera House, Harbour Bridge, Bondi Beach, harbour ferries
goodFor: Harbour views, beaches, coastal walks, food, first-time visitors

image.file: File:Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge Dusk (2) 2019-06-21.jpg
image.alt: The Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge at dusk across the harbour

intro: Sydney sits on one of the world's great natural harbours, a drowned river valley of coves, headlands and islands that runs deep into the city. The British established their first colony here in 1788, on the land of the Eora people, and it grew from a convict settlement into Australia's largest city, with more than five million people.

Two structures define the skyline. The Sydney Opera House, designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973, is one of the most recognisable buildings on earth, with sail-like shells of white tile, and it was inscribed by UNESCO in 2007. The Sydney Harbour Bridge, completed in 1932 and nicknamed the Coathanger, spans the water beside it, and adventurous visitors can climb its arch.

But Sydney is as much about the outdoors as the landmarks. Beaches such as Bondi, Coogee and Manly are a short bus or ferry ride from the centre, cliff-top walks connect them, and ferries are a normal way to commute. It is an expensive city, but a beautiful one, with a relaxed outdoor lifestyle.

whyVisit.intro: Sydney is one of the most beautiful cities in the world, and the easiest introduction to Australia.

points.title: An incredible harbour
points.text: Ferries, sails and headlands, with the Opera House and Harbour Bridge as the backdrop.

points.title: City and beach together
points.text: Surf beaches and coastal walks within half an hour of the centre.

points.title: History and culture
points.text: The Rocks, the Botanic Garden and Aboriginal heritage tours tell layered stories.

points.title: Food and coffee
points.text: A multicultural food scene, harbourside dining and excellent cafés.

points.title: A gateway
points.text: The Blue Mountains, the wine regions and the south coast are easy trips.

attractionsIntro: Most sights cluster around Circular Quay and the harbour, with the beaches a short trip away.

attractions.name: The Sydney Opera House

image.alt: The white sail-shaped roofs of the Sydney Opera House

attractions.text: The great performing arts centre on Bennelong Point, best seen from the water, from the Botanic Garden and from close up. Tours take you inside, or you can see a performance.
attractions.tip: Book a tour or a show in advance.

attractions.name: The Sydney Harbour Bridge

image.file: File:Sydney Harbour Bridge, New South Wales (483531) (9440428703).jpg
image.alt: The steel arch of the Sydney Harbour Bridge over the water

attractions.text: A steel arch bridge that opened in 1932. You can walk across the pedestrian footway for free, or climb the arch with a guide for a panoramic view.
attractions.tip: The BridgeClimb takes about three hours and sells out at weekends.

attractions.name: The Rocks

image.alt: Historic sandstone buildings and streets in The Rocks in Sydney

attractions.text: The oldest part of Sydney, where the first settlers landed, with sandstone buildings, pubs, a Saturday and Sunday market and museums.
attractions.tip: Visit early or in the evening.

attractions.name: The Royal Botanic Garden

image.alt: Lawns and trees in the Royal Botanic Garden beside Sydney Harbour

attractions.text: A free, waterfront garden with lawns, palms and fig trees, ending at Mrs Macquarie's Chair with the best view of the Opera House and Bridge together.
attractions.tip: Walk here from the Opera House.

attractions.name: Bondi Beach and the coastal walk

image.alt: Surfers and swimmers at Bondi Beach in Sydney

attractions.text: The most famous surf beach in Australia, and the start of the 6-km Bondi to Coogee cliff walk, which passes rock pools, coves and sculptures.

attractions.name: Manly and the ferry
attractions.text: A 30-minute ferry from Circular Quay to Manly, a beach suburb with a surf beach, a harbour beach and the Corso, with fine views on the way.
attractions.tip: Sit on the outside deck, on the right side going out.

thingsToDoIntro: Sydney is best enjoyed in the open air, on foot and on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a harbour ferry
thingsToDo.text: Sydney's ferries are working public transport with the best views in the city, to Manly, Taronga Zoo, Watsons Bay and Parramatta.
thingsToDo.tip: Use an Opal card or contactless payment.

thingsToDo.title: Walk from Bondi to Coogee
thingsToDo.text: A coastal path of about 6 km past headlands, beaches and rock pools.
thingsToDo.tip: Start early, and bring sunscreen and water.

thingsToDo.title: Climb the Harbour Bridge
thingsToDo.text: A guided climb of the arch with harnesses, at dawn, day, twilight or night.

thingsToDo.title: See a show at the Opera House
thingsToDo.text: Opera, ballet, concerts and comedy in an iconic setting.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Taronga Zoo
thingsToDo.text: Koalas, kangaroos and a view of the harbour, reached by ferry.

thingsToDo.title: Learn about Aboriginal Sydney
thingsToDo.text: Walking tours by Aboriginal guides in the Botanic Garden and The Rocks explain the history of the Eora.

foodIntro: Sydney's dining is diverse, fresh and casual, with seafood, brunch, Asian food and excellent coffee.

foods.name: Seafood
foods.text: Sydney rock oysters, prawns, barramundi and fish and chips by the harbour.

foods.name: Brunch
foods.text: Smashed avocado, eggs and coffee, served in cafés across the city.

foods.name: Meat pie
foods.text: A traditional pie with a flaky crust.

foods.name: Asian food
foods.text: Excellent Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese and Japanese food, in Chinatown and the suburbs.

foods.name: Flat white and coffee
foods.text: Strong, well-made coffee is the norm.

accommodation.intro: Sydney is expensive, and location matters. Stay near Circular Quay for sights, or in a beach suburb for the coast.

areas.name: Circular Quay and The Rocks
areas.text: Hotels close to the Opera House and harbour.

areas.name: Surry Hills and the CBD
areas.text: Boutique hotels and hostels in lively streets.

areas.name: Bondi and Manly
areas.text: Apartments and guesthouses near the sand.

gettingThere.intro: Sydney is Australia's main international gateway.

options.text: Direct flights from Asia, North America, Europe via hubs and New Zealand, and domestic flights from every state.
options.detail: The airport is connected to the city by train in about 15 minutes.

options.text: About 1 hour 30 minutes by air, or a long overnight train or a day's drive of about 9 hours.
Sydney to Melbourne is about 880 km, and to Brisbane about 920 km.

gettingAround.intro: Public transport is good, and the harbour ferries are part of it.

options.text: An integrated system, paid with an Opal card or contactless card.
Routes to Manly, Taronga Zoo and Watsons Bay.
options.detail: The best way to see the harbour.

options.text: The centre and the coastal paths are walkable.

bestTime.headline: September–November and March–May
bestTime.summary: Sydney has a mild, temperate climate, with warm summers and cool winters.

seasons.text: Warm and sunny, with fewer crowds.
Hot and humid, the peak beach season. Busy and expensive at Christmas and New Year.
Warm, dry days and settled weather.
Cool and mostly sunny, with the Vivid light festival in May and June.

bestTime.avoid: New Year's Eve, unless you want the fireworks and the crowds.

itinerary.title: Three days in Sydney
itinerary.intro: The harbour landmarks, the beaches, and a slower day on the water.

days.title: The harbour
days.morning: The Opera House and the Botanic Garden.
days.afternoon: The Rocks and the Harbour Bridge.

days.title: Beaches
days.afternoon: A swim and lunch at Bondi.

days.title: Ferries and the north
days.afternoon: A walk at Manly and lunch.

tipsIntro: A few tips make Sydney easier and cheaper.
tips: Use an Opal card or contactless payment on public transport.
Take the ferry for the best views. It is public transport, and cheap.
Swim only between the red and yellow flags.
Wear sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses, even on cloudy days.
Book the Bridge Climb and Opera House shows in advance.
Stay near the ferry wharves and stations.
Avoid New Year's Eve unless you plan far ahead.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Sydney?
faq.a: Three days for the highlights, four or five with the Blue Mountains.
Yes, particularly accommodation and eating out. Free attractions such as the beaches, the garden and the ferries help.

faq.q: Is it safe to swim at Bondi?
faq.a: Yes, at the patrolled area between the flags. Rips are common, so follow the lifeguards.

faq.q: Can I walk across the Harbour Bridge for free?
faq.a: Yes, the pedestrian footway on the east side is free.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: September to November and March to May.

faq.q: Is it worth visiting the Blue Mountains?
faq.a: Yes, as a day trip by train, about two hours each way.
